statement_summary: One program aligned to CSF 2.0 and SP 800-82 Rev. 3; TSA directives and approved plans met for designated systems
Group CISO accountable; Cybersecurity Coordinator and alternates for each TSA-designated division
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up to group
Risk acceptance authority by level; High pipeline safety risks treated, not accepted
Supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Divisions document common control inheritance yearly; for TSA divisions it is part of the plan
TSA plan discipline: slips reported in 5 business days; amendment request within 50 days of a permanent change; immediate notice for SD 01G measures
All OT, display, alarm, and controller-facing analytics changes through control room management of change
Annual common control assessment; independent architecture design review; OT Assessment Practice does not assess group divisions
Security terms for third parties; authorized representative contracts name SD measures
Sanctions documented
AI systems registered and approved under the Group AI Standard
TSA compliance records retained at least 3 years and available for inspection
Unique identities; shared accounts only where operationally critical and registered
Shared account passwords changed when a user leaves
Password reset schedule; documented mitigations and dates for components that cannot be reset
Default credentials changed before connection; field device commissioning checklist
MFA for all workforce and remote access; phishing-resistant for administrators; console compensating controls documented
Least privilege; no standing cross-division access
OT remote access only through division gateway tiers with MFA and recording; no persistent vendor tunnels
Just-in-time privileged access through PAM
Termination within 4 hours
Quarterly certification including OT gateway, shared, and service accounts
Annual domain trust review; no corporate administration of servers that receive OT DMZ data
MFA offered to shippers and IDP clients; required for client administrators and all client users by 2027-03-31
Badge-controlled physical access to control rooms, stations, and equipment rooms
Report suspected incidents within 1 hour; controllers act under procedures first
One group severity scale and playbooks; OT not shown clean is Severity 1
IT/OT isolation authority for each operating division
Precautionary segment shutdown decided by the division president on criteria
Notification matrix owned by counsel; one owner per clock per shift (CISA, PHMSA, FERC, SSI, clients, states)
Severity 1 to the disclosure committee within 24 hours; Form 8-K within 4 business days of a materiality determination
Ransom payments need board approval and an OFAC check
Annual TSA plan exercise testing two objectives; annual cross-division exercise with notices, shutdown, and materiality decisions
Evidence preserved with chain of custody and memory images
Restore only from backups verified free of known malicious code
Four classes; SSI, CEII, OT configurations, and sensitive personal data are Restricted
SSI marking, need-to-know, secure storage, intake, destruction, and referral
SSI disclosures reported to TSA promptly
Cross-division sharing of SSI and CEII limited to project excerpts into the receiving SSI store
Encryption at rest and in transit; OT traffic over IT encrypted
Assessment evidence deleted 30 days after engagement close with certificates
No bulk exports of royalty owner or employee personal information; disposal so records are unreadable
Backups separate, scanned, and restore-tested yearly
No Restricted information in unapproved AI tools; never SSI in generative AI
Annual awareness training and quarterly phishing exercises
Role-based OT training; controller training covers cyber-caused abnormal conditions
Only managed devices and scanned media on OT networks
Assessment toolkits encrypted, secured, and wiped at engagement close
Approved AI tools only; qualified review of AI output in deliverables and operations
